- market-researcher:competitive-analysis: Framework for building competitive landscape decks — market positioning, competitor deep-dives, comparative analysis, strategic synthesis. Use when the user asks for a competitive landscape, competitor analysis, peer comparison, market positioning assessment, strategic review, or investment memo deck. Also triggers on "who are the competitors to X", "benchmark X against peers", "build a market map", or any request to systematically evaluate competitive dynamics across an industry.
- market-researcher:comps-analysis: Build institutional-grade comparable company analyses with operating metrics, valuation multiples, and statistical benchmarking in Excel/spreadsheet format.

**Perfect for:**
- Public company valuation (M&A, investment analysis)
- Benchmarking performance vs. industry peers
- Pricing IPOs or funding rounds
- Identifying valuation outliers (over/under-valued)
- Supporting investment committee presentations
- Creating sector overview reports

**Not ideal for:**
- Private companies without comparable public peers
- Highly diversified conglomerates
- Distressed/bankrupt companies
- Pre-revenue startups
- Companies with unique business models
- market-researcher:idea-generation: Systematic stock screening and investment idea sourcing. Combines quantitative screens, thematic research, and pattern recognition to surface new long and short ideas. Use when looking for new ideas, running screens, or conducting thematic sweeps. Triggers on "idea generation", "stock screen", "find ideas", "what looks interesting", "screen for", "new ideas", or "pitch me something".
- market-researcher:pptx-author: Produce a .pptx file on disk (headless) instead of driving a live PowerPoint document — for managed-agent sessions with no open Office app.
- market-researcher:sector-overview: Create comprehensive industry and sector landscape reports covering market dynamics, competitive positioning, key players, and thematic trends. Use for client requests, sector initiations, thematic research pieces, or internal knowledge building. Triggers on "sector overview", "industry report", "market landscape", "sector analysis", "industry deep dive", or "thematic research".
- last30days:last30days: Research what people actually say about any topic in the last 30 days. Pulls posts and engagement from Reddit, X, YouTube, TikTok, Hacker News, Polymarket, GitHub, and the web. Includes a doctor health check to diagnose broken or missing sources.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# .husky/pre-push
3	#
4	# Four responsibilities:
5	#
6	#   1. SCHEMA DRIFT GUARD
7	#      Runs drizzle-kit generate to detect whether any schema changes in the
8	#      unpushed commits lack a corresponding migration file. Blocks the push
9	#      if drift is found.
10	#
11	#   2. JOURNAL INTEGRITY CHECK
12	#      Runs drizzle-kit check (static — no DB connection required) to confirm
13	#      the snapshot JSON and SQL are internally consistent.
14	#
15	#   3. TYPESCRIPT TYPE-CHECK
16	#      Runs tsc --noEmit to catch type errors (e.g. invalid StatusPillColor
17	#      values) before they reach CI. Bypass with SKIP_TYPECHECK=1.
18	#
19	#   4. NEON PREVIEW BRANCH TEARDOWN
20	#      Detects branch deletions (`git push origin --delete <branch>`) and
21	#      tears down the corresponding Neon preview branch automatically.
22	#
23	# ── Emergency bypass ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
24	# If you need to skip the migration checks (e.g. fixing a broken hook itself),
25	# set SKIP_MIGRATION_CHECK=1 before pushing. This is logged locally so there
26	# is an audit trail. The CI migration-check and migration-smoke-test jobs will
27	# still catch any real drift before merge.
28	#
29	#   SKIP_MIGRATION_CHECK=1 git push
30	#
31	# Note: git push --no-verify skips ALL hooks (including Neon teardown). Prefer
32	# SKIP_MIGRATION_CHECK=1 so the Neon teardown still runs on branch deletion.
33	
34	REPO_ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || echo ".")
35	ZERO="0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"
36	
37	# ── 1 & 2. Schema drift guard + journal integrity check ──────────────────────
38	
39	CURRENT_BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "HEAD")
40	
41	# ── Emergency bypass with audit log ──────────────────────────────────────────
42	if [ "${SKIP_MIGRATION_CHECK:-0}" = "1" ]; then
43	  GIT_USER=$(git config user.email 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
44	  TIMESTAMP=$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')
45	  LOG_FILE="${REPO_ROOT}/.git/migration-check-bypasses.log"
46	  echo "${TIMESTAMP} | ${GIT_USER} | branch: ${CURRENT_BRANCH} | SKIP_MIGRATION_CHECK=1" >> "$LOG_FILE"
47	  echo "⚠️  SKIP_MIGRATION_CHECK=1 — migration checks bypassed by ${GIT_USER} at ${TIMESTAMP}"
48	  echo "   Bypass logged to .git/migration-check-bypasses.log"
49	  echo "   CI migration-check and smoke-test jobs will still enforce correctness."
50	else
51	  # Determine the commit range being pushed.
52	  REMOTE_REF="refs/remotes/origin/${CURRENT_BRANCH}"
53	  if git rev-parse --verify "$REMOTE_REF" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
54	    RANGE="origin/${CURRENT_BRANCH}..HEAD"
55	  else
56	    # New branch — compare vs the nearest common ancestor with main/dev
57	    BASE=$(git merge-base HEAD "origin/main" 2>/dev/null \
58	        || git merge-base HEAD "origin/dev" 2>/dev/null \
59	        || git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD)
60	    RANGE="${BASE}..HEAD"
61	  fi
62	
63	  SCHEMA_CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only "$RANGE" 2>/dev/null | grep "^src/lib/schema/" || true)
64	
65	  if [ -n "$SCHEMA_CHANGED" ]; then
66	    # ── Schema drift check via drizzle-kit generate ─────────────────────────
67	    #
68	    # Cleanup strategy: snapshot drizzle/ before the probe runs, then diff
69	    # afterwards to delete ONLY files drizzle-kit created on this run.
70	    #
71	    # A naive `rm -f drizzle/*_pre_push_check.sql` glob silently deletes the
72	    # four legacy committed sentinel stubs from PR #965
73	    # (0036__pre_push_check.sql, 0050_, 0057_, 0067_). That happened on
74	    # 2026-04-24 (b9e2074d → reverted in b1368889). Snapshot-diff avoids it.
75	    #
76	    # Journal handling: we back up _journal.json before the probe and restore
77	    # it afterwards. This preserves any legitimately staged journal changes
78	    # in the push — a blanket `git checkout -- drizzle/meta/_journal.json`
79	    # would discard them.
80	    PROBE_SNAPSHOT_BEFORE=$(mktemp)
81	    find drizzle -type f 2>/dev/null | sort > "$PROBE_SNAPSHOT_BEFORE"
82	    PROBE_JOURNAL_BACKUP=$(mktemp)
83	    cp drizzle/meta/_journal.json "$PROBE_JOURNAL_BACKUP" 2>/dev/null || true
84	
85	    cleanup_probe_artifacts() {
86	      local after_files
87	      after_files=$(mktemp)
88	      find drizzle -type f 2>/dev/null | sort > "$after_files"
89	      # Delete anything that didn't exist before the probe ran.
90	      comm -13 "$PROBE_SNAPSHOT_BEFORE" "$after_files" | while IFS= read -r f; do
91	        [ -n "$f" ] && rm -f "$f"
92	      done
93	      rm -f "$after_files"
94	      # Restore journal to the exact pre-probe state (preserves staged edits).
95	      if [ -s "$PROBE_JOURNAL_BACKUP" ]; then
96	        cp "$PROBE_JOURNAL_BACKUP" drizzle/meta/_journal.json
97	      fi
98	      rm -f "$PROBE_SNAPSHOT_BEFORE" "$PROBE_JOURNAL_BACKUP"
99	    }
100	
101	    # Runs without stdin (</dev/null) so interactive prompts never stall the hook.
102	    DRIFT_OUTPUT=$(npx drizzle-kit generate --name _pre_push_check 2>&1 </dev/null || true)
103	
104	    if echo "$DRIFT_OUTPUT" | grep -q "No schema changes"; then
105	      echo "✓ No Drizzle migration drift detected."
106	      cleanup_probe_artifacts
107	    elif echo "$DRIFT_OUTPUT" | grep -q "generated"; then
108	      cleanup_probe_artifacts
109	      echo ""
110	      echo "╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗"
111	      echo "║  SCHEMA DRIFT DETECTED — push blocked                           ║"
112	      echo "╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣"
113	      echo "║                                                                  ║"
114	      echo "║  src/lib/schema/ changed but no migration file was committed.   ║"
115	      echo "║  The CI migration-check job would also fail.                    ║"
116	      echo "║                                                                  ║"
117	      echo "║  Fix:                                                            ║"
118	      echo "║    npm run db:generate                                           ║"
119	      echo "║    git add drizzle/                                              ║"
120	      echo "║    git commit -m 'chore: add drizzle migration'                 ║"
121	      echo "║    git push                                                      ║"
122	      echo "║                                                                  ║"
123	      echo "║  Emergency bypass (logged, CI still enforces):                  ║"
124	      echo "║    SKIP_MIGRATION_CHECK=1 git push                              ║"
125	      echo "║                                                                  ║"
126	      echo "╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝"
127	      echo ""
128	      exit 1
129	    else
130	      cleanup_probe_artifacts
131	      echo "⚠️  Could not verify migration drift (drizzle-kit returned unexpected output)."
132	      echo "   Verify manually: npm run db:generate"
133	      echo "   Continuing push..."
134	    fi
135	  fi
136	
137	  # ── Journal integrity check (static — no DB connection needed) ─────────────
138	  # drizzle-kit check verifies snapshot JSON + SQL consistency.
139	  # It does NOT require DATABASE_URL or any live DB connection.
140	  MIGRATION_CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only "$RANGE" 2>/dev/null | grep "^drizzle/" || true)
141	
142	  if [ -n "$MIGRATION_CHANGED" ] || [ -n "$SCHEMA_CHANGED" ]; then
143	    CHECK_OUTPUT=$(npx drizzle-kit check --config drizzle.config.ts 2>&1 </dev/null || true)
144	    if echo "$CHECK_OUTPUT" | grep -qi "error\|failed\|invalid"; then
145	      echo ""
146	      echo "╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗"
147	      echo "║  MIGRATION JOURNAL INTEGRITY FAILURE — push blocked             ║"
148	      echo "╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣"
149	      echo "║                                                                  ║"
150	      echo "║  drizzle-kit check found inconsistencies in the migration       ║"
151	      echo "║  journal or snapshot files. Fix before pushing.                 ║"
152	      echo "║                                                                  ║"
153	      echo "║  Output:                                                         ║"
154	      echo "$CHECK_OUTPUT" | sed 's/^/║    /'
155	      echo "║                                                                  ║"
156	      echo "║  Fix:                                                            ║"
157	      echo "║    Inspect drizzle/meta/_journal.json for duplicate entries     ║"
158	      echo "║    or delete the stale snapshot and re-run db:generate          ║"
159	      echo "║                                                                  ║"
160	      echo "╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝"
161	      echo ""
162	      exit 1
163	    else
164	      echo "✓ Migration journal integrity check passed."
165	    fi
166	  fi
167	
168	  # ── Orphan migration file check ───────────────────────────────────────────
169	  # Detects migration SQL files that exist in drizzle/ but have no
170	  # corresponding entry in _journal.json. This prevents the exact bug where
171	  # an agent creates a .sql file but forgets the journal entry, causing the
172	  # migration runner to silently skip it.
173	  if [ -f drizzle/meta/_journal.json ]; then
174	    JOURNAL_TAGS=$(jq -r '.entries[].tag' drizzle/meta/_journal.json 2>/dev/null || true)
175	    ORPHANS=""
176	    for sql_file in drizzle/[0-9]*.sql; do
177	      [ -f "$sql_file" ] || continue
178	      TAG=$(basename "$sql_file" .sql)
179	      # Skip _pre_push_check files (generated by drift detection above)
180	      echo "$TAG" | grep -q "_pre_push_check" && continue
181	      if ! echo "$JOURNAL_TAGS" | grep -qx "$TAG"; then
182	        ORPHANS="${ORPHANS}\n  - ${sql_file} (tag: ${TAG})"
183	      fi
184	    done
185	    if [ -n "$ORPHANS" ]; then
186	      echo ""
187	      echo "╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗"
188	      echo "║  ORPHAN MIGRATION FILES — push blocked                          ║"
189	      echo "╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣"
190	      echo "║                                                                  ║"
191	      echo "║  These migration SQL files have no entry in _journal.json:      ║"
192	      echo -e "$ORPHANS" | sed 's/^/║    /'
193	      echo "║                                                                  ║"
194	      echo "║  The migration runner will SKIP these files silently.           ║"
195	      echo "║                                                                  ║"
196	      echo "║  Fix: Add entries to drizzle/meta/_journal.json, e.g.:          ║"
197	      echo '║    { "idx": N, "version": "7", "when": <epoch_ms>,             ║'
198	      echo '║      "tag": "<filename_without_.sql>", "breakpoints": true }    ║'
199	      echo "║                                                                  ║"
200	      echo "╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝"
201	      echo ""
202	      exit 1
203	    else
204	      echo "✓ No orphan migration files found."
205	    fi
206	
207	    # ── Orphan snapshot check ───────────────────────────────────────────────
208	    # Detects journal entries whose matching drizzle/meta/NNNN_snapshot.json
209	    # file is missing. Surfaced during the 2026-04-23 P0 (Asana
210	    # 1214243524777966) when PRs #2384/#2385/#2397/#2375/#2411 each merged a
211	    # migration SQL + journal entry but never committed the paired snapshot
212	    # JSON. `drizzle-kit check` accepts this state, but the repo's
213	    # validate-drizzle-journal.js (which gates dev→main promotion) fails on
214	    # any snapshot missing for a journal idx greater than main's max idx.
215	    ORPHAN_SNAPSHOTS=""
216	    # Read all journal indices into a newline-separated list of zero-padded ids.
217	    JOURNAL_IDX=$(jq -r '.entries[].idx' drizzle/meta/_journal.json 2>/dev/null || true)
218	    for idx in $JOURNAL_IDX; do
219	      PADDED=$(printf '%04d' "$idx")
220	      if [ ! -f "drizzle/meta/${PADDED}_snapshot.json" ]; then
221	        ORPHAN_SNAPSHOTS="${ORPHAN_SNAPSHOTS}\n  - drizzle/meta/${PADDED}_snapshot.json (journal idx ${idx})"
222	      fi
223	    done
224	    if [ -n "$ORPHAN_SNAPSHOTS" ]; then
225	      echo ""
226	      echo "╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗"
227	      echo "║  ORPHAN SNAPSHOT FILES — push blocked                           ║"
228	      echo "╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣"
229	      echo "║                                                                  ║"
230	      echo "║  Journal entries reference these snapshot files, but they do    ║"
231	      echo "║  not exist on disk:                                              ║"
232	      echo -e "$ORPHAN_SNAPSHOTS" | sed 's/^/║    /'
233	      echo "║                                                                  ║"
234	      echo "║  drizzle-kit generate writes both the SQL file AND its matching ║"
235	      echo "║  snapshot JSON. If you committed only the SQL, the snapshot is  ║"
236	      echo "║  lost. The dev→main promotion validator will fail.              ║"
237	      echo "║                                                                  ║"
238	      echo "║  Fix: re-run drizzle-kit generate and commit the _snapshot.json ║"
239	      echo "║  files alongside the .sql files. If the schema has drifted,     ║"
240	      echo "║  see docs/hadp-v3/ for the snapshot-restore pattern.            ║"
241	      echo "║                                                                  ║"
242	      echo "╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝"
243	      echo ""
244	      exit 1
245	    else
246	      echo "✓ No orphan snapshot files found."
247	    fi
248	  fi
249	
250	  # ── Migration index conflict check ──────────────────────────────────────────
251	  # Detects when this branch creates a migration with the same index number
252	  # as one already on the base branch (dev/main) but with a different tag name.
253	  # This prevents the merge conflict we hit when two branches independently
254	  # generate the same migration number.
255	  if [ -n "$MIGRATION_CHANGED" ]; then
256	    # Determine the upstream base branch
257	    TARGET_BASE=""
258	    for candidate in origin/dev origin/main; do
259	      if git rev-parse --verify "$candidate" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
260	        TARGET_BASE="$candidate"
261	        break
262	      fi
263	    done
264	
265	    if [ -n "$TARGET_BASE" ]; then
266	      BASE_JOURNAL=$(git show "${TARGET_BASE}:drizzle/meta/_journal.json" 2>/dev/null || echo '{"entries":[]}')
267	      HEAD_JOURNAL=$(cat drizzle/meta/_journal.json)
268	
269	      CONFLICT_FOUND=""
270	      TMPENTRIES=$(mktemp)
271	      echo "$HEAD_JOURNAL" | jq -r '.entries[] | "\(.idx):\(.tag)"' > "$TMPENTRIES"
272	      while IFS= read -r entry; do
273	        [ -z "$entry" ] && continue
274	        IDX=$(echo "$entry" | cut -d: -f1)
275	        TAG=$(echo "$entry" | cut -d: -f2-)
276	        BASE_TAG=$(echo "$BASE_JOURNAL" | jq -r --arg idx "$IDX" '.entries[] | select(.idx == ($idx | tonumber)) | .tag' 2>/dev/null || true)
277	        if [ -n "$BASE_TAG" ] && [ "$BASE_TAG" != "$TAG" ]; then
278	          CONFLICT_FOUND="yes"
279	          echo "  Index ${IDX}: ${TARGET_BASE} has '${BASE_TAG}', local has '${TAG}'"
280	        fi
281	      done < "$TMPENTRIES"
282	      rm -f "$TMPENTRIES"
283	
284	      if [ -n "$CONFLICT_FOUND" ]; then
285	        echo ""
286	        echo "╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗"
287	        echo "║  MIGRATION INDEX CONFLICT — push blocked                        ║"
288	        echo "╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣"
289	        echo "║                                                                  ║"
290	        echo "║  This branch reuses a migration index that already exists on    ║"
291	        echo "║  ${TARGET_BASE} with a different name.                          ║"
292	        echo "║                                                                  ║"
293	        echo "║  Fix:                                                            ║"
294	        echo "║    1. git fetch && git merge ${TARGET_BASE}                     ║"
295	        echo "║    2. Renumber your migration to the next available index       ║"
296	        echo "║    3. Update _journal.json and the snapshot filename            ║"
297	        echo "║    4. Run: drizzle-kit check to verify consistency              ║"
298	        echo "║                                                                  ║"
299	        echo "╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝"
300	        echo ""
301	        exit 1
302	      else
303	        echo "✓ No migration index conflicts with ${TARGET_BASE}."
304	      fi
305	    fi
306	  fi
307	fi
308	
309	# ── 3. TypeScript type-check ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
310	#
311	# Catches TS errors (e.g. invalid StatusPillColor values, wrong arg types)
312	# before they reach CI. This runs ONCE per push, not per commit, so the
313	# latency hit is acceptable. Bypass with SKIP_TYPECHECK=1 for emergency pushes
314	# (CI will still catch real errors).
315	
316	if [ "${SKIP_TYPECHECK:-0}" != "1" ]; then
317	  echo "Running TypeScript type-check..."
318	  # Run tsc and capture output. Exclude .next/ — it contains auto-generated
319	  # validator stubs that go stale when routes are added/removed and are not
320	  # real source errors.
321	  TSC_OUTPUT=$(npx tsc --noEmit --project "${REPO_ROOT}/tsconfig.json" 2>&1)
322	  SRC_ERRORS=$(echo "$TSC_OUTPUT" | grep "error TS" | grep -v "^\./\.next/\|^\.next/" || true)
323	  if [ -n "$SRC_ERRORS" ]; then
324	    echo "$SRC_ERRORS"
325	    echo ""
326	    echo "╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗"
327	    echo "║  TYPECHECK FAILED — push blocked                                ║"
328	    echo "╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣"
329	    echo "║                                                                  ║"
330	    echo "║  Fix the TypeScript errors above before pushing.                ║"
331	    echo "║  Bypass: SKIP_TYPECHECK=1 git push (CI will still catch errors) ║"
332	    echo "║                                                                  ║"
333	    echo "╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝"
334	    exit 1
335	  fi
336	  echo "✓ TypeScript type-check passed."
337	fi
338	
339	# ── 4. Neon preview branch teardown ──────────────────────────────────────────
340	
341	while IFS=' ' read -r localref localsha remoteref _remotesha; do
342	  # A zero SHA for the local side means this is a branch deletion
343	  if [ "$localsha" = "$ZERO" ]; then
344	    BRANCH=$(echo "$remoteref" | sed 's|refs/heads/||')
345	
346	    # Skip protected branches
347	    case "$BRANCH" in
348	      main|dev|uat-preview|HEAD) continue ;;
349	    esac
350	
351	    bash "${REPO_ROOT}/scripts/neon-branch-delete.sh" "$BRANCH"
352	  fi
353	done
